title: Kenafric feedback submission (v1.0)
description: The body of a POST to WF-14 (kenafric-wf14), for every one of the five feedback instruments. Four keys and nothing else: additionalProperties is false, so a stray key is rejected rather than ignored. Validated against real payloads by src/feedback/payload.test.ts with Ajv — against this file, not against the app's opinion of it.

t.description: The signed token from the link, passed through verbatim. base64url payload, '.', base64url HMAC-SHA256. The app never decodes it: a claim read from an unverified token is a claim the recipient could have rewritten. n8n verifies it against LINK_SECRET. It is also the idempotency key — WF-14 stores it as Response Token and refuses one already on the list.

formType.description: Which instrument this is, echoed back from what the context endpoint said. Never a value the browser chose. WF-14 branches on it and maps it to the Form Type option name.

submittedAt.description: ISO 8601 with the local UTC offset, never Z. Every one of these is submitted in Nairobi, and a 09:00 EAT response filed as 06:00 UTC reads as somebody answering before the email went out.

answers.description: The answers, keyed by ClickUp custom field id. This is the decision the whole layer rests on: WF-14 carries no question-text mapping table, so rewording a question never breaks it and a new instrument needs no workflow change. Sparse — an unanswered optional question is ABSENT, never null and never an empty string, because an empty string is a value ClickUp will write and 'skipped' reports differently from 'answered nothing'.

propertyNames.description: A complete ClickUp custom field UUID. An abbreviated id is refused here rather than guessed at: a wrong id writes a real answer to the wrong field, and neither that nor a silent drop fails loudly.

oneOf.description: A five-star (ClickUp emoji) answer. An integer 1-5, which is what the API takes and returns.

Everything else: a drop_down option NAME, or a text answer. Never an option UUID — those change if anyone rebuilds a field, and a public bundle has no business holding one. WF-14 resolves the name against the live field schema. Trimmed, and never empty.
